text:
Montreal arrives in St. Louis short-handed but winning. The Canadiens beat Winnipeg 2-1 on Sunday and are 3-1-1 in their last five, all without Nick Suzuki and Ivan Demidov. Oliver Kapanen has taken Suzuki's spot beside Juraj Slafkovský and Cole Caufield, and Noah Dobson has moved onto the first power-play unit. St. Louis is coming off a 4-0 loss to Carolina, where Pyotr Kochetkov stopped all 24 shots, and is 2-3-0 in its last five.

The numbers say there isn't much between them. At five on five, MTL has taken 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games to STL's 49%, and our model has it close to a toss-up, 2.96 to 3.06 for the home side. Montreal's weak spot is discipline: it takes 5.4 penalties a game, which keeps feeding power plays. In net, projected starters Jacob Fowler (+6.0 goals saved above expected, meaning goals he stopped beyond what the shots should have produced) and Joel Hofer (+3.2) both sit above average this season. Fowler has been hot, going 5-0-0 over his last five starts. Hofer's track record is longer, at +11.1 last season over 46 games.

Caufield is our top Montreal pick, with a 36% chance to score and 60% to get a point. He had assists on the first two goals against Winnipeg, as Karine Hains of The Hockey News posted. Josh Anderson plays his 700th NHL game. For St. Louis, Jimmy Snuggerud (29% to score) and Dylan Holloway (26%, with a 60% shot at a point) lead the way.
